newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM TO SELL FURTHER ASLK STAKE TO FORTIS - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM TO SELL FURTHER ASLK STAKE TO FORTIS - PAPER.

text.p: The Belgian government plans to sell a further 24.8 percent stake in banking group ASLK-CGER to Belgian-Dutch insurance and banking group Fortis, Belgian financial daily L'Echo said on Tuesday.
The paper said that, contrary to expectations, the government would not use its put option on Fortis, but try to negotiate a direct sale.

Under a 1993 deal by which Fortis bought an initial 49.9 percent of ASLK for 34 billion francs, the government can sell Fortis a further 9.8 percent of the bank. Fortis also has a first right of refusal on a further 15 percent of the bank.
L'Echo said the put option's exercise price was seven billion francs, plus six percent per year since 1993, valuing it now at about 8.4 billion francs.
But the paper said the present value of the 9.8 percent stake was well above 8.4 billion.

The paper said that based on an estimated full-year 1996 net profit of nearly 10 billion francs and a price/earnings ratio of 10, the whole bank was worth about 100 billion francs, thus a 9.8 percent stake would be worth about 10 billion.

The paper gave no time frame for the transaction, but said that a possible partial ASLK bourse listing would have to wait until after this autumn, because of an ongoing capital increase at Generale Bank and a planned partial bourse listing of publicly-owned bank Credit Communal/Gemeentekrediet (CCB) will already siphon a lot of capital to the bank sector.
Spokesmen at the Belgian finance ministry, Fortis and ASLK all said they could not immediately comment on the article.
This afternoon, Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene presents his 1997 budget, which may shed more light on the government's plans with ASLK.
